corrective_scope: Responds to the independent audit findings F1-F6 against the Batch 10.4 Fourth Corrective packaging delivery. No Batch 10.5 work performed. No UI, clipboard, download, backup, restore, Prompt Pack, rendered-image, persistence-write, or external-integration work performed.

findings_addressed.F1: hasScopePolicyViolation (new) rejects a shape-valid plan that selects an artifact category its own resolved scope.policy disallows (e.g. an Output A injected into an output_b/group_b/cover/execution_plan package). The prior relational checks proved selected artifacts were mutually consistent with each other, but never checked whether a category should have been selected at all under the resolved scope's own policy flags - a single internally-consistent Output A (e.g. the scene's own genuine record) satisfied every relational check and slipped through. This check runs first, before hasDuplicateScopeIdentifiers/hasRelationalIntegrityViolation, and fails closed with the registered EXPORT_SCOPE_001 code.
findings_addressed.F2: hasRelationalIntegrityViolation now anchors every selected/referenced output id to plan.scope.outputAIds/outputBIds - the resolved scope's own flat ground-truth allowlists, computed once by resolveExportScope directly from the source project, never touched by selection/numbering construction. Two jointly-forged-but-mutually-consistent fields (e.g. Output B's sourceOutputAId and its numbering row's outputAId, both set to the same fabricated value) now fail because that value is not a real, in-scope id, not merely because the fields disagree with each other. A reverse-uniqueness claim map additionally rejects a real, in-scope id being claimed by more than one (sessionId, sceneId) identity, closing the case where a selected Output A whose id belongs to a different in-scope scene is jointly forged into another identity's slot. One residual, explicitly documented limitation remains: a fully bijective exchange of two real ids between two in-scope identities (every dependent field on both sides re-forged together) cannot be distinguished from a legitimate assignment using only the flat, per-category existence allowlists this contract exposes - see the completion report and the corresponding test's block comment for the full rationale (closing it would require a schema change to the frozen ExportResolvedScope contract, or re-deriving from the source project inside packaging, both out of scope).
findings_addressed.F3: hasDuplicateScopeIdentifiers (new) rejects a duplicated real id in plan.scope.sessionIds/groupIds/outputAIds/outputBIds/coverIds/versionIds before content is built - closing the case where scope.sessionIds = [sameSession, sameSession] caused the same real session to be re-emitted under two different ordinal folders. scope.sceneIds is deliberately excluded from this check: a SceneId is only guaranteed unique within its own session, so a complete_project/all-scope plan spanning two sessions that happen to reuse a scene id string legitimately produces that duplicate in this flat, session-less array - rejecting it would have broken the audit's own required C5 same-sceneId matrix, since content construction is keyed by the complete (sessionId, sceneId) identity throughout and a repeated scene-id string alone cannot cause double-emission.
findings_addressed.F4: The ZIP verifier's canonical local/central physical-order check is now a dedicated pass (reused-offset check, then a central-order monotonicity scan, then coverage: prefix/overlap/gap/final) run strictly before the coverage checks, rather than one combined pass. Previously, a real interior local-block swap was reported as local_entry_gap and a full reversal as unexpected_archive_prefix - both real rejections, but not the exact local_order_mismatch reason the physical-order disagreement actually represents, because the old combined pass could reach a forward-gap or non-zero-first-offset anomaly before it ever saw the backward jump that proves the order violation. Both cases now assert exactly structural/local_order_mismatch.
findings_addressed.F5: Adds a genuine same-sceneId cross-session adversarial matrix (5 items: both sessions valid; session 2 has no selected A/B; session 2 B points at session 1's A; session 2 numbering forged to session 1's ids; array order reversed) using one literal SceneId string reused across two real, independent sessions. The Fourth Corrective's twoSessionPairPlan() helper (used by its 'cross-session reused-identity scopes' tests) gave each session a distinct scene id and never actually exercised the reused-sceneId condition its own tests claimed to cover; those tests are unchanged (they still validate real, useful behavior over distinct-scene-id sessions) and this new, separate matrix closes the literal reused-sceneId gap the audit identified.
findings_addressed.F6: Delivers the completion report as its own standalone Markdown file (this delivery's PHASE10-BATCH10.4-FIFTH-CORRECTIVE-COMPLETION-REPORT.md), alongside the checkpoint ZIP + sha256, CHANGED-FILES-MANIFEST.md, and INDEPENDENT-VERIFIER-TEST-EVIDENCE.md - five files as required, none of them a screenshot or an inline-only description.
